Authentication accepted a SQL tautology payload and returned an authenticated-looking response.

Potential Harm

Injection can expose or modify application data and may unlock administrative access depending on query context.

Use strict parameter binding, reject unsafe query fragments, and remove SQL error/data leakage from responses.

20. Brute-force protection gap: POST /Login

HIGHEst. CVSS: 8.1Status: validatedConfidence: 0.80

state-mutation, rce-adjacent
Attempted
yes
Impact Bound
max 50 request(s) per vector; 15s request timeout; single canary mutation where required

yes

no

Finding Overview

Multiple rapid login attempts did not trigger visible rate-limit or lockout controls.

Potential Harm

Remote command execution could allow an attacker to run server-side commands, pivot to adjacent services, or alter application data.

Example Validation

Send 8 failed login attempts to http://[REDACTED_HOST]/Login and confirm no 429/lockout response.

Evidence

8 rapid failed attempts completed in 0.19s with statuses [200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200].

Remediation

Enforce account/IP rate limits, progressive backoff, and temporary lockouts on repeated failures.

Remediation

Implement token revocation or short-lived tokens with rotation and server-side invalidation checks.

24. Admin-route access unlocked by the bypass

Finding Overview

A validated authentication or role bypass unlocked adjacent admin or privileged routes during the same run.

Potential Harm

Broken authorization can expose privileged data or operations to users who should not be able to reach them.

Example Validation

Replay the validated bypass, then compare unauthenticated and bypass-authenticated access to the recorded admin route.

- Unauthenticated sensitive endpoint exposure: GET /rest/admin/application-configuration (high, validated)

- IDOR signal: GET /api/Users/:id (high, validated)
- Admin role injection during registration (critical, validated)
- SSRF internal fetch signal: /profile/image/url (high, validated)

Remediation

Fix the underlying primitive findings in this capability chain and retest the chained access path.

Different password-reset/security-question responses indicate whether an account exists.
